messages:
maria: Heads-up — I just noticed a mismatch between Console per-session cost and the ledger for a resumed streaming request after a region fallback. Tokens are showing up under a new session_id, console still groups by session_id so totals diverge. Anyone seen this?

sam: Yep, saw something similar on the canary yesterday. Resume path appears to generate a fresh session_id. Traces sometimes carry provenance_id but our console query uses session_id as the grouping key. :thinking:

lee: Confirmed. Ledger rows are keyed by provenance_id (tracelet/provenance) and console aggregates by session_id. When resume creates a new session_id the link breaks even though provenance is the same.

ashley: Quick question — are toolcall tokens also affected? If a toolcall happens mid-resume do tokens go to the old session or the new one?

lee: Toolcalls are attributed to whatever session_id is on the active stream at the time of the toolcall. If a handoff occurs mid-stream you'll end up with tokens split across session_ids but same provenance. That makes reconciliation annoying.

maria: Here are a couple of real log lines from the repro run: 
```
[INFO] resume.start session_id=abcd1234 provenance=prov-7f
[INFO] resume.assigned session_id=efgh5678 provenance=prov-7f tokens_received=120
```
You can see provenance stays prov-7f but session_id flips. Console query that sums tokens by session_id will miss the earlier abcd1234 chunk.

sam: So root cause: billing/console join keys are inconsistent. Ledger uses provenance_id, Console uses session_id. Because resume allocates a new session_id we need a stable join key surfaced everywhere.

ashley: Proposal: short-term — emit prev_session_id (or parent_session_id) on resume.assigned events and have the console fallback to provenance_id or parent_session when session continuity is low. Long-term — pick a canonical "provenance" field for billing and make both subsystems join on that.

maria: Agreed. For a patch I can: (1) add prev_session_id to resume events, (2) update the console query to union on provenance_id when present, (3) add a unit test showing resume->new-session still aggregates. I'll open a PR.

sam: @ashley can you loop in billing here? We might need to run a reconciliation job and decide if refunds are needed for affected customers.

ashley: cc @billing-bot — can you run a reconciliation for provenance=prov-7f over the last 24h and give us the delta (ledger vs console)?

billing-bot: billing-bot: queued job reconcile_prov prov-7f window=24h. ETA ~ 12m. Will DM CSV when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria: Thanks — I'll also add an alert to ingestion that fires when resume creates a new session_id without parent_session set (counts > 0 over 5m). That should catch regressions during rollouts.

lee: Also recommend a small UX change: console tooltip explaining provisional vs confirmed charges and why small deltas can appear during region failovers. Avoid freaking out users.

maria: Good call. I'll add the tooltip text to the PR description.

ashley: For followups: (a) PR for resume event schema + console query patch, (b) reconciliation run results, (c) decide on refunds if delta > threshold.

maria: I'll post the PR link here in a bit. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
